key_insight: A learned cross-embodiment sensor-conversion model translates large-scale, in-the-wild video (e.g., dashcams) into the sensor modalities and configurations used by autonomous vehicle fleets, enabling reuse of diverse real-world data for ADS training and validation.
problem_solved: Addresses the data scarcity and domain-mismatch between proprietary AV fleet sensors and abundant but unstructured in-the-wild footage — unlocking long-tail, geographic, and behavioral diversity for autonomous driving systems without requiring massive new fleet collection.
method: Train a neural conversion model that maps observations across sensor modalities and vehicle embodiments (e.g., dashcam → multi-camera/LiDAR-like outputs), preserving geometric and semantic consistency.
Combine geometry-aware modules with cross-modal consistency objectives and adversarial/domain-adaptation losses so converted outputs are realistic and usable by downstream ADS pipelines.
Leverage a mix of limited paired fleet data and large-scale unpaired in-the-wild video using cycle/consistency and self-supervised signals to generalize across viewpoints, cameras, and vehicles.
impact: Makes abundant dashcam and in-the-wild data practical for improving ADS robustness, coverage of long-tail events, and validation, reducing dependence on costly fleet data collection and accelerating model generalization.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: source in-the-wild dashcam input → sensor-conversion network → target fleet sensor outputs (multi-camera / synthetic LiDAR), annotated with training signals (paired/unpaired, consistency losses).
Before/after example panels: raw dashcam frame vs. converted multi-view images / depth or LiDAR-lookpoint visualization to show fidelity and preserved semantics.
Dataset coverage map or icon grid: scale + diversity of dashcam sources (regions, weather, long-tail scenarios) contrasted with limited fleet coverage.
Bar/line chart: downstream task improvements (e.g., detection / segmentation / mapping) when training on converted data vs. baseline.
paper_title: Sensor2Sensor: Cross-Embodiment Sensor Conversion for Autonomous Driving
paper_authors: Jiahao Wang, Bo Sun, Yijing Bai, Vincent Casser, Songyou Peng
